key_insight: Model slicing turns a single large LLM into heterogeneous smaller collaborators that can re-check each other’s reasoning steps and reduce error propagation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical way to improve reasoning accuracy and inference efficiency without relying on one monolithic model or expensive RL-based multi-agent systems.
method: Construct heterogeneous collaborator models via model slicing under a comparable parameter budget.
Use pyramid supervision to combine protocol distillation with step-level step supervision.
Learn when and how models should interact so they can reassess prior reasoning across distinct parameterizations.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on multi-hop QA, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and constrained generation, and the trained heterogeneous models matched or exceeded the original large model and multi-agent baselines while using higher inference efficiency.
watch_item: Performance depends on effective training of collaboration policies and may be sensitive to task/domain shifts where heterogeneous model disagreements are less informative.
paper_title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
